title: Publicly offered card terms vary across products in APR, credit-tier pricing, fees, and rewards
source_unit: US credit-card product and issuer records in the CFPB Terms of Credit Card Plans survey

denominator.unit: product rows in the CFPB TCCP spreadsheet after the metadata/header rows

unique_issuers.unit: unique institution names among product rows

unique_products.unit: unique product names among product rows

top_25_issuer_rows.unit: product rows marked as issued by a top-25 institution

purchase_apr_offered.unit: product rows marked Yes among 663 rows

credit_tier_apr_variation.unit: product rows marked Yes for purchase APR varying by credit tier

observations.method: Reproducible spreadsheet inspection with header row 10 selected, product-row counts, unique institution/product counts, and categorical field tabulation; no weighting or population inference.
observations.uncertainty: Rows are product offers submitted to the statutory survey, not transactions, approvals, cardholders, or market shares. Institution/product names may not be unique economic entities; missing fields are retained and counts describe the file surface only.
observations.subgroup: Products marked top-25 versus other institutions; card products with and without credit-tier-varying purchase APR.
observations.counterinterpretation: A broad product menu does not imply equal availability: eligibility, geography, credit score, income, underwriting, and actual take-up can narrow the options presented to a household.

denominator.unit: product rows with purchase APR offered Yes

median_purchase_apr.unit: percent; median of numeric purchase APR median field

median_purchase_apr_min.unit: percent; median of numeric purchase APR minimum field

median_purchase_apr_max.unit: percent; median of numeric purchase APR maximum field

apr_zero_values.value: some rows report zero or promotional/conditional values

observations.method: Descriptive tabulation of numeric CFPB TCCP purchase-APR fields; percentages converted from spreadsheet decimal representation and rows with nonnumeric/missing fields excluded from each statistic.
observations.uncertainty: These are advertised plan terms, not realized APRs paid by account holders. The product-level median is not a market-weighted or borrower-weighted average; credit-tier, balance, promotion, and eligibility conditions matter.
observations.subgroup: Products with a purchase APR offer; many products separately report APR variation by credit tier.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower advertised minimum may be available only to stronger applicants, while a higher maximum may never be assigned; the range is not a within-person price change.

observations.period: 2025-07-01 to 2025-12-31; product fees, promotions, and rewards

denominator.unit: TCCP product rows; each field retains its own nonmissing universe

annual_fee_reported.unit: product rows with a numeric annual-fee value

median_annual_fee.unit: US dollars among numeric annual-fee values

rewards_missing_or_unreported.unit: product rows with missing Rewards field

cashback_rewards.unit: product rows whose Rewards text includes cashback rewards

observations.method: Descriptive tabulation of categorical, numeric, and text fields; reward count searches the product-level Rewards field and is not a measure of reward value or take-up.
observations.uncertainty: Some fields are blank, textual, conditional, or product-specific. Reward presence does not measure generosity; a late-fee offer does not show a fee paid; and an annual-fee value does not establish total cost.
observations.subgroup: Product offers with introductory APR, balance transfer, late-fee, annual-fee, and rewards fields; top-25 status is retained in the file.
observations.counterinterpretation: Fees can fund services or rewards, promotions can provide short-run liquidity, and consumers can avoid or repay some charges. Product terms alone do not establish household burden or issuer conduct.

related_sources.claim: Direct CFPB TCCP spreadsheet for the July-December 2025 reporting period.
CFPB market report provides aggregate 2024 card cost and balance context.

boundary: This record is a product-offer surface, not a cardholder, transaction, approval, or market-share estimate. Product terms can condition access and future cost, but the record does not establish which household received which term, what was paid, or whether a consumer could switch or obtain a remedy.
